detailed_rationale:
Sterling & Wilson Renewable Energy (formerly Sterling & Wilson Solar) is a global solar EPC and O&M provider (27.3 GWp EPC, 13.5 GWp O&M across 28 countries), and the fundamentals here show multiple, genuine red flags rather than a stale-data quirk. FY26 ended with a consolidated net loss of Rs 296 Cr, and the Sep 2025 quarter alone showed a Rs 478 Cr loss driven by a Rs 469 Cr negative other-income swing -- a real, disclosed one-off that we cannot characterize further from the sources available but that clearly dominated that quarter's result. ROE and ROCE are both negative (-14% and -12% in our data), and while Mar 2026 and Jun 2026 showed a partial return to profit (Rs 142 Cr and Rs 53 Cr respectively), margins remain thin (5-7% OPM) for an EPC business.

Beyond the P&L, the balance-sheet and governance signals are the more serious concern: Acuite downgraded or withdrew ratings on Rs 7,575 Cr of bank facilities as recently as July 2026, 27.6% of promoter holding is currently pledged, and promoter stake itself has nearly halved over several years (77.2% in Mar 2020 to 45.7% by Jun 2026). A Senior VP of Investor Relations also resigned in July 2026. Individually some of these might be explainable; stacked together (rating action, meaningful pledge, halved promoter stake, executive departure, a large one-off loss quarter) they describe a company still working through real financial stress, not merely a cyclical EPC business having an off year.

The global solar EPC/O&M order-book opportunity is real and structurally growing, and if the company stabilizes its balance sheet the operating franchise (scale, geographic diversification, O&M annuity book) has value -- but we would want to see the rating situation resolved and the pledge materially reduced before treating this as more than a Sell.
recommendation_rationale: Sell, following the quant score -- negative return ratios, a large one-off loss quarter, a recent rating downgrade/withdrawal on a large facility, and a meaningful promoter pledge are precisely the combination of red flags our framework is designed to catch; we see no basis to rescue this to Hold this round.
summary: Sterling & Wilson Renewable Energy is a global solar EPC and operations-and-maintenance provider that posted a net loss for FY26, including one quarter dominated by a large one-off financial swing. More concerning, a rating agency downgraded or withdrew ratings on a large chunk of the company's bank facilities in July 2026, and more than a quarter of promoter shares are currently pledged. We rate it a Sell: the global solar EPC opportunity is real, but the balance sheet and credit signals here need to stabilize before this looks investable on fundamentals.
positive_para: The company has real scale and global reach in solar EPC and O&M (27.3 GWp EPC and 13.5 GWp O&M across 28 countries), operates in a structurally growing global renewable-energy build-out market, and showed a partial return to quarterly profitability in Mar 2026 and Jun 2026 after the Sep 2025 loss.
negative_para: FY26 closed with a net loss, driven partly by a Rs 469 Cr one-off negative swing in a single quarter; more seriously, Acuite downgraded or withdrew ratings on Rs 7,575 Cr of bank facilities as recently as July 2026, 27.6% of promoter shares are pledged, and promoter ownership has nearly halved since 2020. A senior Investor Relations executive also resigned in July 2026. This combination of signals describes real, ongoing financial stress rather than a routine cyclical rough patch.
reverse_dcf_judgment: With negative trailing returns on capital and a recent rating downgrade/withdrawal on a large slice of its bank facilities, this is not a name we can value on a conventional multiple basis -- the market is pricing a turnaround narrative (global EPC scale, O&M annuity book) that the credit-rating action and promoter pledge level both argue is not yet secured. We would need to see the rating situation stabilize and the pledge come down materially before treating any current price as attractive.
